industry.structure: Three state oil marketing companies (IOC, BPCL, HPCL) sell most of India's petrol, diesel and LPG at prices set in practice with the Government; Reliance and Nayara are export-oriented private refiners with smaller retail networks; MRPL (ONGC group) and CPCL (IOC group) are standalone refiners. HPCL is the smallest refiner of the three OMCs but has the third-largest retail network (25,098 outlets) and is the second-largest LPG marketer (ar26).
industry.pricing: Petrol and diesel prices are formally deregulated but were held for long stretches, including through the 2026 Gulf war; household LPG is sold below cost and compensated case by case (₹7,920 cr for HPCL conveyed in Oct-2025 for under-recoveries to Mar-2026). Losses on LPG not yet compensated sit off the balance sheet in a 'negative buffer' (₹16,410 cr for HPCL at Jun-2026).
industry.war2026: US-Iran conflict from end-Feb 2026: Strait of Hormuz disrupted; Brent averaged ~US$105/bbl in Q1FY27 vs US$76 in Q4FY26 (BOB); diesel cracks ~US$50/bbl and petrol ~US$25 (BOB). The Government cut excise (SAED) on petrol and diesel by ₹10/litre in Mar-2026, re-imposed export duties, and allowed retail price rises in tranches from May. The three OMCs lost money on fuel marketing in Q1FY27; refiners and HPCL's refining arm earned record cracks, part of which the export duty took away.
industry.src: ar26; bob; pl; IOC research file (industry facts, sourced there)

competition: HPCL refines ~24.5 MMTPA itself (Mumbai, Visakh) against ~51 MMT of sales, the lowest refining cover of the OMCs (IOC ~31% of India's refining with ~42% of sales; BPCL is closer to balanced). The gap is filled from JV refineries (HMEL, MRPL, and from Jul-2026 HRRL) and third parties, so HPCL earns relatively more of its profit, and loses more in a squeeze, on marketing.

street.methodView: Three of the four notes that disclose a method value HPCL on EV/EBITDA of standalone EBITDA (6.0x on Dec-27E to Jun-28E) plus investments (MOSL also values HRRL and HMEL; BOB and Emkay add only the listed MRPL and Oil India stakes); PL uses 1.1x FY28E book. We follow the EV/EBITDA sum of the parts of the IOC template and show P/E and DCF as cross-checks.

moat: Network rather than refining: 25,098 fuel stations, 6,389 LPG distributors, pipelines (25.5 MMT) and terminals in the west and south, plus offtake rights over JV refineries (HMEL, HRRL). Refining is mid-sized (24.5 MMTPA own; Visakh now 11.6 Nelson complexity). None of it protects margins: prices are administered, the product is a commodity, and the most marketing-heavy OMC is the first to bleed when prices are held.
critiques: HPCL's marketing tilt makes it the most exposed OMC when retail prices are held: Q1FY27 loss ₹12,265 cr against IOC's ₹1,631 cr.
Leverage: gross debt rose from ₹47,600 cr to ₹72,600 cr in one quarter (debt/equity ~1.4-1.5x), and HRRL's ~₹53,000 cr of project debt sits off balance sheet.
HRRL cost nearly doubled to ₹79,459 cr and came ~4 years late; returns on HPCL's ₹19,600 cr equity are unproven.
The Vizag residue upgrade did not run stably in Q1; its GRM uplift (~US$2.5/bbl) is still a promise.
Governance: one independent director on an 8-member board; Audit Committee out of compliance; parent ONGC and the Ministry decide.
